sections.title: Explanation
sections.content: An adjective placed after the noun, as the predicate, agrees with it in number (szék nagy → székek nagyok), but the same adjective in its usual position before the noun never changes. Quantity words like sok ('many') and néhány ('a few') are always followed by a singular noun.

items.english: There are several books on the table.

sections.content: Több does double duty for 'more' and 'several', and either way it still takes a singular noun: több könyv, not több könyvek. If you're ever unsure whether a quantity word wants a singular or plural partner, singular is the safer default — most of them (sok, néhány, több) work this way.
